facts.statement: The genus Jibeinia has been proposed as a possible synonym for the genus Vescornis.
A local farmer presented the holotype fossil of Jibeinia to an engineer in the summer of 1993.
facts.quote: In the summer of 1993, the holotype was presented to engineer Li Pai of the Hebei Provincial Office of Geology by a local farmer.

facts.statement: Researchers investigated the quarry at the Dongtuyao brick factory in Northern Hebei Province where the fossil was found.
facts.quote: Li, along with Hou Linhai and Zhou Zhonghe, investigated the quarry from which it came, at the locality of the Dongtuyao brick factory, Northern Hebei Province, Linjituxiang Village.

facts.statement: Initial research placed the fossil in the Yixian Formation, but later geological studies showed it came from the similarly aged Huajiying Formation.
facts.quote: They determined that it was collected from the Yixian Formation. However, later research into the geology of the area showed that it actually came from similarly aged beds of the Huajiying Formation.

facts.statement: The species Jibeinia luanhera was described based on a nearly complete fossil.
facts.quote: J. luanhera was described from a nearly complete fossil.

facts.statement: The holotype fossil never received a catalogue number or was accessioned by a museum.
facts.quote: The fossil seems not to have ever received a catalogue number, nor to have been accessioned by a museum.

facts.statement: The original holotype fossil of Jibeinia is currently lost.
Jibeinia lived during the Early Cretaceous period.
The genus Jibeinia was reclassified by O'Connor et al. in 2016.
Jibeinia is classified within the family Gobipterygidae.
Jibeinia is an extinct genus of avialan belonging to the clade Enantiornithes.
facts.quote: Jibeinia es un género extinto de avialano perteneciente al clado Enantiornithes.

facts.statement: Jibeinia lived between the Barremian and Aptian stages, approximately 125.77 to 119.57 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Aptian (125.77 to 119.57 million years ago)

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that Vescornis might be a junior synonym of Jibeinia, but this cannot be confirmed without rediscovering the lost holotype.
facts.quote: Thus they conclude that it will be impossible to rule out the possibility that the two are the same species, and that Vescornis is a junior synonym, unless the holotype of Jibeinia is rediscovered.
